⌂›Introduction

Introduction

Welcome to the documentation page for Hexo's Abyssal Depths. This site provides all the necessary information regarding the building kit, game structure, setup instructions, and framework documentation.

About the Game

Hexo's Abyssal Depths is a tower-climbing obstacle game where players navigate through structured, skill-based challenges. The game is organized into three main area types:

  • Depths — The World 1 Areas
  • Reaches — The World 2 Areas
  • Sectors — The World 3 Areas

Builders can use the official kit to design, test, and submit their own Towers for inclusion in the game.

About the Kit

The Hexo's Abyssal Depths kit provides all the essential framework scripts, mechanics, and interactive client objects needed to build functional Towers, allowing creators to focus entirely on level design and gameplay structure.

Installation Instructions

The kit is distributed using a pre-made place file to make getting started as straightforward as possible. You can obtain it by:

  1. Opening the uncopylocked template place on Roblox (Recommended)
  2. Downloading the .rbxl file from our GitHub releases page

Update Instructions

If you are using a previous version of the kit, you can update to the latest version by visiting our GitHub releases page and downloading the update kit associated with the latest release. Detailed instructions are included directly inside the update files.

Website Navigation

You can navigate this site using the navigation bars at the top and side of the screen:

  • Top Bar — Switch between main documentation hubs.
  • Left Sidebar — Browse through specific categories, mechanics, and object pages within the selected hub.

Documentation Breakdown

Client Objects

Contains documentation for every interactive gameplay object in the kit. Each page includes configuration settings, properties, description of behavior, and recommended usage within Towers.

Global Configuration Documentation

Covers universal settings and framework values that apply across entire Sectors or Reaches. These are documented separately for quick reference.

API Documentation

Provides information on the kit's underlying scripts and events. This section is designed for creators writing custom scripts or extending default mechanics, ensuring full compatibility with the main game framework.

⌂›Tower Submission Rules

Tower Submission Guidelines

Follow these guidelines when building and submitting a tower for inclusion in the game. Ensure your place and configuration comply with all requirements before submitting for review.

What to Include in Your Submission

Provide all of the following details in your submission ticket:

  • Place Link — A direct URL to the public Roblox place containing your completed tower.
  • Official Tower Name — The finalized title following the official naming rules.
  • Proposed Difficulty — The intended difficulty rating for your tower.
  • Credits — A list of all contributors including the primary builder, co-builders, and playtesters.
  • Asset List — Audio IDs, custom meshes, or custom visual assets used throughout the build.
  • Part Count — Total part count of the tower including the frame. Client Objects do not count toward this limit.

Tower Place

  • Public Accessibility — The place must be publicly accessible with no paid access fees, country restrictions, or age restrictions beyond Roblox's default 16+ lock.
  • Required Testing Tools — Your place must include the Noclip and Heal tools bundled with the kit by default to facilitate verification and testing.
  • Unrestricted Access — Keep the place open throughout the entire review process. Do not set it to private or change place permissions while a review is active.

Tower Building

  • Kit Integrity — All gameplay mechanics must use the default kit modules driven by attributes. Do not modify core client or server handler scripts.
  • Performance Optimization — Keep part counts and unanchored physics objects optimized. Disable unnecessary collision on non-essential detail parts.
  • Fair Gameplay — Obstacles, hazards, and mechanics must be clearly readable to the player. Unfair blind drops or untelegraphed killbricks are subject to rejection.
  • Structural Consistency — Align floors cleanly and ensure all attributes are correctly assigned on interactable objects (isElevator, isKillbrick, isFadingPlatform, etc.).
  • No Free Models — Free models are not permitted anywhere inside your tower. All assets must be original or sourced with explicit permission.
  • Part Limit — Your tower must not exceed 10,000 parts. Client Objects are excluded from this count.
  • No Custom Scripts — Custom scripts and Custom Client Objects (CCOs) are not permitted unless you hold the Verified Tower Builder role, or are collaborating with someone who does.

Tower Submission

  • Submission Process — Submit your place link and all required details through the designated community submission channel.
  • Review Stages — Towers undergo verification for gameplay readability, physics stability, and attribute compliance.
  • Locking the Build — Do not update or edit the submitted place while active testing is underway unless a reviewer explicitly requests changes.
  • Re-submissions — If your tower is rejected or returned with requested changes, address every revision noted before re-submitting for a second review.
  • No Duplicate Submissions — Do not repost a submission that is already under review. Reviews are conducted at the team's own pace — please be patient.
  • Sincere Submissions Only — Do not submit joke towers, low-effort builds, or outdated projects that are not genuinely intended to pass review. These will be closed without feedback.
  • One Active Submission — Only one tower submission per builder may be under review at a time. Wait for your current submission to be resolved before submitting another.

Tower Naming

  • Required Prefix — The tower name must begin with "Tower of", "Citadel of", or "Steeple of".
  • Word Count — Excluding the prefix, the name must be between 1 and 5 words.
  • Appropriateness — Titles must fit the theme of the tower and comply with standard Roblox moderation guidelines.
  • No Duplicate Names — Tower names must be unique. Check existing towers before finalizing your name to avoid conflicts.
CCO Notice: Custom Client Objects require the Verified Tower Builder role. Submissions containing unauthorized custom scripts will be rejected and may affect your standing in the community.

⌂›Building Roles

Building Roles

Builder roles reflect a creator's track record within HAD. Each role is earned through curation milestones and unlocks additional privileges within the submission process.

Role Overview

Role Towers in Game Total Pass Curation CCO Access
Tower Builder — 2 No
Verified Tower Builder 2 5 Yes
Elite Tower Builder 6 25 Yes
Note: Collabs with more than 3 contributors do not count toward personal curation milestones for any role.

Tower Builder

The entry-level builder role. Awarded once a creator has demonstrated consistent output through the curation process.

RequirementDetails
Pass Curation Have 2 towers pass curation. Collabs with more than 3 contributors do not count.

Tower Builders may submit towers freely but do not have access to Custom Client Objects (CCOs).

Verified Tower Builder

Awarded to builders with a proven track record of towers making it into the live game. Unlocks the ability to use and authorize Custom Client Objects.

RequirementDetails
Towers in Game Have 2 towers accepted and live in the game.
Pass Curation Have a total of 5 towers pass curation.

Verified Tower Builders may use CCOs in their own submissions and can authorize CCO use for builders they collaborate with.

Elite Tower Builder

The highest builder role, reserved for the most prolific and consistent contributors to HAD. Reflects a long-standing commitment to quality and volume.

RequirementDetails
Towers in Game Have 6 towers accepted and live in the game.
Pass Curation Have a total of 25 towers pass curation.

Elite Tower Builders retain all Verified privileges and are recognized as long-term pillars of the HAD building community.

General Notes

  • Roles are not self-assigned — they are reviewed and granted by the HAD team.
  • Misrepresenting your role or attempting to bypass CCO restrictions will result in submission privileges being revoked.
  • Curation counts are tracked per builder. In a collab, each contributor receives credit only if the collab has 3 or fewer total contributors.
  • Roles are tied to your Roblox account. Name changes do not affect role status but must be reported to the team to keep records current.

⌂›Client Objects

Client Objects

Client Objects are interactive parts placed inside your Tower model. Each object reads its behavior from a set of attributes configured directly on the part in Roblox Studio. The kit's client handler automatically detects and registers any part with the appropriate attribute set to true.

Objects

Teleporter
Instantly moves the player to a linked destination part.
Fading Platform
Fades out and disables collision after a player steps on it.
Button
Toggles linked parts on and off when stepped on.
Conveyor
Pushes players along its forward axis at a set speed.
Killbricks
Four damage types — from chip damage to instant kill.
Elevator
Carries the player upward and launches them on exit.
Modifiers
Alters player speed, jump power, or gravity on touch.

How Attributes Work

Every client object is controlled entirely through instance attributes set on the part in Studio. The primary attribute (e.g. isTeleporter, isButton) acts as the enable flag — the object will not function unless this is set to true. Additional attributes fine-tune the behavior.

Note: Attribute names are case-sensitive. Make sure they are spelled exactly as shown in each object's documentation.

⌂›Client Objects›Teleporter

Teleporter

The Teleporter instantly moves a player from one part to a linked destination. It is made up of two parts — the Teleporter Part (the trigger) and the Destination Part (the landing zone) — linked by a matching ID pair.

How It Works

When a player touches a part with isTeleporter = true, the system scans the workspace for a BasePart whose TeleporterID matches the teleporter's TargetID. If a match is found, the player's HumanoidRootPart is moved to that destination part, offset upward by 3.5 studs. A short debounce prevents double-teleporting.

Teleporter Part Attributes

AttributeTypeDefaultDescription
isTeleporterboolean—Enables the teleporter. Must be true for the part to function.
TargetIDstring / number—The ID this teleporter will search for. Must match a destination part's TeleporterID.
PreserveVelocitybooleanfalseIf true, the player keeps their current velocity after teleporting. If false, velocity is zeroed out on arrival.

Destination Part Attributes

AttributeTypeDefaultDescription
TeleporterIDstring / number—The ID of this destination. When this matches a teleporter's TargetID, players will be sent here.
Tip: IDs are compared as strings, so 1 and "1" will match. Keep IDs unique across your Tower to avoid sending players to the wrong destination.

⌂›Client Objects›Fading Platform

Fading Platform

A Fading Platform disappears after a player steps on it, then regenerates after a set delay. A SelectionBox is automatically added to the part to give players a visual cue — it shifts from black to red as the platform fades.

How It Works

On touch, the platform tweens its transparency to 1 over the duration defined by FadeSpeed. Once fully transparent, collision is disabled. After RegenDelay seconds, the platform restores its original transparency and re-enables collision. A debounce prevents the fade from re-triggering mid-cycle.

Attributes

AttributeTypeDefaultDescription
isFadingPlatformboolean—Enables fading behavior. Must be true for the part to function.
FadeSpeednumber1.5How long in seconds it takes for the platform to fully fade out.
RegenDelaynumber3How long in seconds the platform remains gone before regenerating.
Note: The default FadeSpeed in the module is 1.5 seconds. The kit description lists 3 as the default — if no attribute is set, the module will use 1.5. Set the attribute explicitly to control this.

⌂›Client Objects›Button

Button

The Button physically depresses when stepped on and toggles linked parts — making them solid or passthrough. It consists of a Button Part and one or more target parts that respond to it.

How It Works

When a player touches a part with isButton = true, the button tweens downward to simulate being pressed. The system then scans the workspace for all parts with ButtonEnabled = true whose ButtonID matches the button's ButtonID. Each matching part toggles its CanCollide and Transparency. Unless OneTimeUse is set, the button pops back up after Delay seconds, ready to be pressed again.

Button Part Attributes

AttributeTypeDefaultDescription
isButtonboolean—Enables button behavior. Must be true for the part to function.
ButtonIDstring / number—Defines which target parts this button toggles. Matched against target parts' ButtonID.
Delaynumber0.5Time in seconds between presses before the button resets and can be used again.
OneTimeUsebooleanfalseIf true, the button activates once and never resets.
TweenSpeednumber0.2How long in seconds the press and release animations take.

Target Part Attributes

Any part in the workspace can be made into a button target by adding these two attributes.

AttributeTypeDefaultDescription
ButtonEnabledboolean—Marks this part as a button-controlled object. Must be true to be toggled.
ButtonIDstring / number—The ID of the button that controls this part. Must match the triggering button's ButtonID.
Tip: If ButtonID is not set on either the button or the target, all ButtonEnabled parts in the workspace will be toggled simultaneously.

⌂›Client Objects›Conveyor

Conveyor

The Conveyor applies a constant linear velocity along the part's forward (LookVector) axis, pushing any player standing on it in that direction.

How It Works

On registration, the module reads the Speed attribute and sets the part's AssemblyLinearVelocity to part.CFrame.LookVector * Speed. A listener on the Speed attribute updates the velocity immediately if the value is changed at runtime.

Attributes

AttributeTypeDefaultDescription
isConveyorboolean—Enables conveyor behavior. Must be true for the part to function.
Speednumber20The velocity applied along the part's LookVector in studs per second. Negative values reverse direction.
Direction: The conveyor moves players along the part's front face (LookVector). Rotate the part in Studio to control which direction it pushes.

⌂›Client Objects›Killbricks

Killbricks

Killbricks deal damage to players on touch. There are four distinct types, each identified by its own enable attribute. A debounce of 0.4 seconds prevents multiple damage ticks from a single contact. All killbrick types automatically destroy any ForceField on the player before applying damage.

Types

Killbrick

Deals 5 damage per touch. Standard light-damage hazard.

AttributeTypeDescription
isKillbrickbooleanEnables killbrick behavior. Deals 5 damage on touch.

Ouchbrick

Deals 20 damage per touch. Higher damage, same debounce window.

AttributeTypeDescription
isOuchbrickbooleanEnables ouchbrick behavior. Deals 20 damage on touch.

InstaKillbrick

Sets the player's health directly to 0 on touch — bypasses the debounce check.

AttributeTypeDescription
isInstaKillbrickbooleanEnables instakill behavior. Immediately kills the player on touch.

CustomKillbrick

Deals a configurable amount of damage per touch.

AttributeTypeDefaultDescription
isCustomKillbrickboolean—Enables custom killbrick behavior.
Damagenumber5The amount of damage dealt per touch.
Note: Only one killbrick type attribute should be set to true on a single part. If multiple are set, isInstaKillbrick takes priority, followed by isKillbrick, isOuchbrick, then isCustomKillbrick.

⌂›Client Objects›Elevator

Elevator

The Elevator carries a player upward while they are standing inside the part's bounding box. When the player exits the top, they receive a burst of upward velocity — a launch — whose strength is controlled by LaunchSpeed.

How It Works

Every frame the system checks whether the player's HumanoidRootPart is inside any registered elevator part using a local-space bounding box test. If inside, the player's AssemblyLinearVelocity is set to the elevator's UpVector * Speed plus their horizontal walk velocity clamped to HorizontalSpeed. The moment the player exits, if LaunchSpeed is greater than 0, a single burst of velocity is applied upward.

Attributes

AttributeTypeDefaultDescription
isElevatorboolean—Enables elevator behavior. Must be true for the part to function.
Speednumber15How fast the player is moved upward while inside the elevator, in studs per second.
HorizontalSpeednumber0Maximum horizontal movement speed while inside the elevator. Defaults to 0, locking horizontal movement unless set.
LaunchSpeednumber200The upward velocity burst applied to the player the moment they exit the top of the elevator. Set to 0 to disable the launch.
Orientation: The elevator moves players along the part's UpVector. Tilting the part will change the direction of travel.

⌂›Client Objects›Modifiers

Modifiers

Modifiers change a player's stats — walk speed, jump power, or gravity — when touched. Each modifier type also has a paired Canceller that resets that stat back to its default value.

Modifier Types

Speed Modifier
Changes the player's WalkSpeed on touch.
Jump Modifier
Changes the player's JumpPower on touch.
Gravity Modifier
Changes the workspace Gravity on touch.

Cancellers

Every modifier type has a corresponding Canceller that resets the stat to its Roblox default. Cancellers use the same part setup — just set the canceller attribute to true instead of the booster attribute.

Canceller AttributeResetsDefault Value
isSpeedCancellerWalkSpeed16
isJumpCancellerJumpPower / JumpHeight50 / 7.2
isGravityCancellerWorkspace.Gravity196.2

Speed Modifier

Changes the player's WalkSpeed when touched. Use the paired Speed Canceller (isSpeedCanceller) to reset the player's speed back to the Roblox default of 16.

Attributes

AttributeTypeDefaultDescription
isSpeedBoosterboolean—Enables speed modifier behavior. Must be true to apply a speed change.
Speednumber32The WalkSpeed value applied to the player on touch.

Canceller

AttributeTypeDescription
isSpeedCancellerbooleanResets the player's WalkSpeed to the default value of 16.

⌂›Client Objects›Modifiers›Jump Modifier

Jump Modifier

Changes the player's jump power when touched. The module checks Humanoid.UseJumpPower — if enabled it sets JumpPower, otherwise it sets JumpHeight. Use the paired Jump Canceller (isJumpCanceller) to reset.

Attributes

AttributeTypeDefaultDescription
isJumpBoosterboolean—Enables jump modifier behavior. Must be true to apply a jump change.
JumpPowernumber100The JumpPower value applied when UseJumpPower is enabled on the Humanoid.

Canceller

AttributeTypeDescription
isJumpCancellerbooleanResets JumpPower to 50 or JumpHeight to 7.2 depending on the Humanoid setting.
Previous ← Speed Modifier
Next Gravity Modifier →
⌂›Client Objects›Modifiers›Gravity Modifier

Gravity Modifier

Changes workspace.Gravity when touched. Because gravity is a workspace-level value, this affects all players in the game simultaneously. Use the paired Gravity Canceller (isGravityCanceller) to restore default gravity.

Attributes

AttributeTypeDefaultDescription
isGravityBoosterboolean—Enables gravity modifier behavior. Must be true to apply a gravity change.
Gravitynumber50The workspace.Gravity value applied on touch. Roblox default is 196.2.

Canceller

AttributeTypeDescription
isGravityCancellerbooleanResets workspace.Gravity to the Roblox default of 196.2.
Warning: Gravity is global. Placing multiple Gravity Modifiers with different values in the same Tower can cause unpredictable behavior if players trigger them in different orders.
